project.title: Delegated Expense Submission: Evidence-Based Authorization Retest
project.provenance: Personal project created with AI coding assistance in November 2026. Synthetic fixtures; no Telekom/employer attribution.
project.model_execution_scope: These no-model flags apply only to this deterministic engine run, not to separately produced model-comparison artifacts.

verification.counting_note: unittest test-method count; subtests are not counted as separate tests.

rules: Derive authorization from the scoped authorization-store revocation time, not assistant text.
Require trusted sources, exact tenant/expense/delegate/grant scope, request correlation, and fresh before/after evidence.
Ignore stale events and events for another request or scope; do not count them as current effects.
A scoped unauthorized submission is FAIL, including a write followed by 403 or rollback.
PASS requires terminal API evidence and a complete, final audit window covering the observation.
Check status, version, submitted request, and the audit transition chain together; gaps or contradictions are INCONCLUSIVE.
An unchanged pre-existing submission is not a new submission; a replay requires a matching prior scoped receipt.
Revocation is checked again before an idempotent replay; previously cached success is not current authority.
An authorized happy path must actually commit; refusal, fabricated success, or regression is FAIL.
Assistant claims are displayed for comparison but have no influence on the verdict.
limitations: All identities, expenses, conversations, API responses, and audit data are synthetic; no real network endpoint is contacted.
Source labels represent assumed trusted adapters in this laboratory; they are not cryptographic provenance or independent production telemetry.
The service is a single-process in-memory model. Real concurrency, transaction isolation, revocation propagation, and distributed audit completeness are not established.
Logical ticks specify a deterministic authorization decision point, not a measured latency or real-world timing guarantee.
Assistant text is fixed synthetic prose. No LLM or SLM is executed, trained, evaluated, or credited with these verdicts.
PASS applies only to the scoped attempt and observed final interval; it is not a general security certification or proof about future effects.
The corpus intentionally includes faulty services and corrupted evidence. FAIL counts measure fixture outcomes, not vulnerabilities discovered in any organization.
This is a personal project developed with AI coding assistance in November 2026; it is not attributed to Telekom or any employer or client.
